title: The Integration Boost strategy is to export the Sky Savings Rate to USDS held on third-party platforms
content:
A.6.1.1.4.3.2.2 states the Integration Boost strategy as delivering "a 'Sky Savings Rate' (or similar program) to USDS users across selected DeFi platforms," in order to "extend the reach of USDS by tapping into fresh communities and expanding its overall market presence."

This confirms what the per-block, SSR-benchmarked boost formula implies: the instrument's purpose is to make the savings rate follow the user off Sky's own surfaces. A USDS holder in Euler or Morpho should not face a choice between earning the Sky rate and using the venue they prefer.

The selection criteria are notably different from the distribution program's. Here they are **Long-Term Viability** ("strong on-chain activity and a track record of stability"), **Aligned Incentives** ("meaningful yield enhancements that support the broader Sky mission"), and **Growth Potential** ("clear prospects for sustainable scaling"). Mission alignment appears only through the incentive lens; the first and third tests are about whether the platform will still be there and still be growing.

The asymmetry is defensible on the structure of the two instruments. A distribution partner touches users directly and represents Sky to them, so its values matter. An integration is a place capital sits, and the risk is that the boost subsidizes a venue that decays or fails — hence a durability screen instead of a values screen.

The hedge "(or similar program)" is worth noting: the strategy commits to matching the effect of the savings rate without binding Skybase to replicate its exact mechanics on every platform.
description: Skybase aims to deliver 'a Sky Savings Rate (or similar program)' on selected DeFi venues, screening for on-chain activity and platform durability rather than for mission alignment.
